Thoracic Clinic Letter
Al Waseem Coast Hospital | 24 February 2026
Re: Saif Hamdan Al Rumaithi, male, DOB 1962-04-17
Emirates ID: 784-1962-5839146-2
Dear Dr Al Nuaimi,
Mr Al Rumaithi attended today following referral from Jisr Al Noor Screening Centre; LDCT dated 03 February 2026 showed a 24 mm spiculated right upper lobe nodule.
CT-guided core biopsy on 17 February demonstrated invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive.
His case was discussed at our thoracic MDT on 23 February. The recommendation was surgical assessment for resection, with oncology review to coordinate management.
Referrals to thoracic surgery and medical oncology have been sent. I explained the diagnosis and proposed pathway to him and his wife in clinic.
Dr Mariam Rashid Al Harthi, Consultant Respiratory Physician

Wadi Al Noor Hospital — Department of Radiology
CT Pulmonary Angiography
Khalifa Hamad Al Ketbi; M; born 1958-11-03; EID 784-1958-7416280-2
Acquired 09/03/2026; authorised 10/03/2026
Clinical details: Acute pleuritic pain and hypoxaemia. Assess for pulmonary embolism.
Acquisition: IV contrast pulmonary arterial phase with multiplanar reformats. DLP 296 mGy.cm. No comparison study.
Pulmonary arterial opacification is satisfactory. No embolus through the subsegmental branches.
Mild dependent atelectasis. Incidental 6 mm solid right upper lobe nodule, series 5 image 84. No adenopathy or pleural effusion.
Conclusion: No pulmonary embolism. For the incidental nodule, recommend chest CT in 6–12 months, guided by clinical risk.
Dr Rashed Al Mehairbi, Specialist Radiologist
